payload.explanation: Glass contamination in chemical solutions is a safety hazard — the entire volume must be discarded and the teacher informed.

payload.snippet: The chromatography experiment was running well when another group accidentally knocked the solvent container off the bench, and some solvent splashed onto her hands.
options: rinse her hands immediately with large amounts of cold water and tell the teacher what solvent it was
wipe her hands on a paper towel and continue the experiment
wait to see whether her skin reacted before telling anyone
use hand sanitiser to neutralise the chemical on her skin
payload.explanation: Unknown solvent contact requires immediate water rinsing and teacher notification — hand sanitiser does not neutralise most organic solvents.

payload.snippet: He was burning food samples to measure their energy content and noticed that one food produced a black smoke that made several students cough.
options: stop the burning immediately, ventilate the room, and check whether the food was safe to burn in a school lab setting
open one window and continue since smoke meant high energy content
burn the sample faster to reduce total smoke time
ask the students coughing to leave the room and continue
payload.explanation: Black smoke from combustion can contain toxic compounds — stopping the burn, ventilating, and verifying the experiment's safety with the teacher are all required.

payload.snippet: She collected six data points for her pendulum experiment but one value was so different from the others that the range of her data was misleading and the average was being pulled far from the typical value.
options: collect additional data points, recalculate, and investigate the anomalous result separately
remove the anomalous value from all calculations without discussion
calculate two averages — one with and one without the outlier — and explain both in the report
round the anomalous value to the nearest typical result
payload.explanation: Reporting dual averages (with and without an outlier) with explanation is a transparent scientific approach that shows understanding of the data's limitations.

payload.snippet: The class was testing how exercise affects breathing rate, but during data collection he noticed that one participant was hyperventilating before the exercise began due to nervousness.
options: note the participant's baseline as elevated due to anxiety and treat it as a confounding factor in the analysis
exclude the nervous participant entirely from the data set
ask the participant to breathe more slowly to bring their rate down before testing
use their data as normal since they still exercised the same way
payload.explanation: Anxiety-elevated baselines affect the measured change in breathing rate — transparent notation as a confounding factor is more honest than exclusion.

payload.snippet: She was writing her conclusion when she realised her data supported one explanation, but she had read a published study that suggested a completely different mechanism was responsible.
options: present both explanations, note that her data agreed with one, and acknowledge that further investigation would be needed to resolve the discrepancy
change her conclusion to match the published study since scientists must know better
ignore the published study since her data was from her own experiment
state that the published study was probably wrong
payload.explanation: Scientific conclusions can acknowledge conflicting explanations — presenting the evidence and noting the discrepancy demonstrates genuine scientific thinking.

payload.snippet: The food dye in the paper chromatography experiment was not separating into multiple colours even after the solvent had risen to the top of the paper.
options: hypothesise whether the solvent type, paper quality, or dye composition could explain the lack of separation
assume the experiment had failed and get new materials
wait longer by adding more solvent until something separated
record 'no separation' and leave it without further investigation
payload.explanation: No separation is a result that needs an explanation — hypothesising about solvent polarity or dye composition turns a 'failed' experiment into genuine learning.

payload.snippet: He was testing electrical circuits and his bulb stopped lighting partway through the experiment even though the battery was new.
options: check each connection and component systematically to identify the fault
replace the entire circuit from scratch
assume the battery had failed and get a new one without checking
record that the circuit stopped working without investigating further
payload.explanation: Systematic fault-finding (checking connections, then bulb, then battery in order) is a core electronics skill — replacing everything without diagnosis wastes resources and teaches nothing.

payload.snippet: She was leading a group of younger children on a farm trail when they came across a field with a footpath that crossed through a herd of cows with calves — a combination explicitly warned against in farm safety guidance.
options: turn the group around and find an alternative route rather than crossing through the herd
cross quickly in a tight group, walking steadily
split the group and cross in pairs to reduce disturbance to the herd
shout and clap to move the cows aside before crossing
payload.explanation: Cows with calves are protective and unpredictable — farm safety guidance explicitly recommends not crossing fields with calves regardless of how calm the herd appears.

payload.snippet: He was watching the farmer use a power take-off shaft on a tractor when a scarf one child was wearing blew loose and drifted toward the rapidly spinning shaft.
options: shout a warning immediately and ensure the child moved away from the shaft at once
grab the scarf himself to pull it clear
run toward the shaft to catch the scarf
call out to the farmer to stop the tractor while the child moved toward the scarf
payload.explanation: Power take-off shafts can entangle loose clothing in a fraction of a second — the priority is getting the person away, not saving the scarf.

payload.snippet: The farm visit group was using a slurry-surrounded footbridge when one child lost her footing and fell into the shallow edge of the slurry tank.
options: pull her out immediately, move her far from the tank, remove contaminated clothing, and call for a farmer and emergency services
rinse her in the nearest water trough to clean the slurry off
tell her to walk carefully to the farmhouse to wash
get the farmer to assess the situation before moving her
payload.explanation: Agricultural slurry contains pathogens including E. coli and Cryptosporidium — immediate removal from the liquid and emergency assessment are required regardless of the volume of exposure.

payload.snippet: She found an injured pheasant in the farmyard that was unable to fly and appeared to have a broken wing.
options: find the farmer and let them assess whether to call a wildlife rehabilitator
try to splint the wing using sticks and her shoelace
put it in a warm dark box she found in the barn
leave it where it was since wildlife should fend for itself
payload.explanation: Wild injured birds require professional handling — moving them incorrectly worsens injuries, and a farmer can advise whether a local wildlife rehabilitator should be called.

payload.snippet: He noticed that the water in a drinking trough one section of the flock was using was green with algae bloom, and the sheep in that area seemed lethargic.
options: report the green water and the lethargic animals to the farmer immediately
clean out the trough himself using a stick to stir out the algae
move the lethargic sheep to the other water trough
take a water sample in his bottle to show the teacher
payload.explanation: Blue-green algae in farm water troughs produces toxins that can rapidly kill livestock — immediate farmer alert prevents further animal exposure.

payload.snippet: During a farm stay visit the group noticed a strong smell of gas near the grain storage building and the farmer was inside operating machinery.
options: shout loudly to alert the farmer immediately and ensure no one entered the building or operated any switches nearby
enter quickly to find the source of the smell
text the farmer since shouting might startle him near machinery
wait outside and call a plumber
payload.explanation: Gas near machinery creates an explosion risk from sparks — shouting is faster than texting and keeping everyone away from switches is critical.

payload.snippet: She was collecting samples from a sheep dip trough as part of a water-quality study when she realised she had accidentally splashed the chemical solution onto her forearm.
options: rinse the arm immediately with large amounts of clean water and tell a teacher and the farmer
wipe the solution off with her sleeve
finish collecting the sample before dealing with the splash
rinse it briefly and monitor for redness during the visit
payload.explanation: Sheep dip chemicals can include organophosphates — immediate prolonged water rinsing and adult notification are the correct responses.

payload.snippet: He was moving hay bales with a farm volunteer using a sack trolley when the bale shifted and fell sideways, pinning his foot against the stone wall.
options: stay calm, call for help, and don't attempt to lift the bale himself
drag his foot free by pulling hard
try to tip the bale back with his other foot
tell the volunteer to go get help while he held the bale steady
payload.explanation: Attempting to free a pinned limb alone risks further injury — calling for help and waiting for assistance is correct.

payload.snippet: She was assigned to help a farm hand spread fertiliser pellets on a field using a broadcast spreader when the wind suddenly shifted and carried a cloud of fertiliser dust directly toward her face.
options: stop the spreader immediately, hold her breath, and walk upwind before breathing normally again
pull her jumper over her nose and continue spreading
duck down below the cloud level and keep working
accelerate the spreader to get the pellets down before the wind got worse
payload.explanation: Agricultural fertiliser dust irritates airways and eyes — stopping the source and moving upwind prevents exposure. Running the spreader faster worsens the cloud.

payload.snippet: He was in the grain store helping to shovel grain from a pile when he noticed the grain surface near him beginning to move in a slow circular pattern beneath his feet.
options: step backward immediately off the grain and exit the store without hesitating
step to the side and continue shovelling from a different angle
call out to the worker at the other end of the store to come and look
crouch down to feel how deep the movement extended
payload.explanation: Grain engulfment happens in seconds and is difficult to reverse — the moving surface is a warning sign requiring immediate exit. Even calling to a colleague takes too long.

payload.snippet: During a farm machinery demonstration a hydraulic hose on the front loader began leaking under high pressure, and she could see a fine mist spraying from the fitting.
options: alert the farmer immediately from a distance and ensure no one moved close to the mist
wrap a cloth tightly around the fitting to stop the leak
reach in to tighten the fitting manually while the engine was running
watch from a short distance to see how bad the leak got
payload.explanation: High-pressure hydraulic mist can penetrate skin and cause serious internal injuries — distance and immediate expert intervention are essential.

payload.snippet: He was bottle-feeding a calf that suddenly became agitated, butted its head hard against his chest, and knocked him against a gate post.
options: tell the farmer and ask for a first-aid check before continuing any animal handling
take a short rest and continue the feeding since calves were often unpredictable
hand the bottle to another child since the calf had taken a dislike to him specifically
finish feeding the calf quickly from a safer distance
payload.explanation: A blow to the chest or back from an animal can cause internal bruising without obvious symptoms — a first-aid check before continuing is the right response.

payload.snippet: The class was watching an electric fence demonstration when the farmer briefly turned off the power to allow them to step over, but while he was explaining something one child reached out and touched the wire before the farmer confirmed it was safe.
options: tell the farmer and check the child for any signs of shock before they moved on
observe whether the child seemed fine and say nothing
test the fence yourself to check whether the power was still off
reassure the child it was probably off and carry on
payload.explanation: Electric fence contact even from a brief touch can cause a muscle reaction that throws the person back — checking for shock symptoms and telling the farmer is always correct.

payload.snippet: She was learning to drive a small tractor under supervision and stalled it on a slope, and the farmer told her to restart it, but she was uncertain whether the handbrake and gear were correctly set before turning the key.
options: confirm verbally with the farmer that the vehicle was in gear and handbrake on before restarting
restart the engine quickly before the tractor moved further
apply extra brake pressure herself while turning the key
ask the farmer to restart it himself to be safe
payload.explanation: Tractor restarts on slopes require confirmed gear engagement and handbrake — a verbal check before restarting is a few seconds that prevents rollback.

payload.snippet: During a farm walk he came across a dead badger at the edge of a field, and some younger children in the group moved toward it out of curiosity.
options: stop them firmly, keep everyone clear, and tell the farmer immediately
check the badger from a short distance to see if it had any obvious cause of death
let the children look from very close range since badgers were harmless when dead
bury the badger quickly so the children didn't get upset
payload.explanation: Dead wildlife can carry disease including bovine tuberculosis in badgers — keeping distance and alerting the farmer is the correct public health response.

payload.snippet: She noticed that several pigs in one pen were biting each other's tails and that one pig had a bleeding wound, but the farmer was in a different building across the yard.
options: find the farmer immediately rather than waiting for the next activity break
separate the injured pig herself by opening the pen divider
distract the pigs by throwing food into the pen
report it at the end of the visit since it was nearly lunchtime
payload.explanation: Tail biting in pigs can escalate rapidly and cause serious injury — finding the farmer immediately is more important than the visit schedule.

payload.explanation: Scorch marks plus frayed cable means unplug and tell adults.

payload.snippet: Walking home alone you realise someone has been walking the same route behind you for several streets, and your road has very few people around at this time.
options: step into the nearest open shop and phone home from there
start running and don't look back until home
turn round and ask them loudly what they want
take a long shortcut through the alley behind the flats
payload.explanation: Open shops give you adults, light, and a phone in seconds.

payload.snippet: Your friend shows you a new vape his older brother left at home and offers you a quick try so you can both say you've done it once.
options: say no and suggest doing something else together instead
try one puff because once won't really count
take it home to show your parents what he's doing
agree but only if he tries it first to check it's safe
payload.explanation: Saying no once is easier than trying to stop later.

payload.snippet: At a music festival with your family you get separated from your parents in the crowd and your phone is on three percent battery near a busy stage.
options: go to the nearest stewards' tent and ask them to find them
keep walking through the crowd shouting for them
use your last battery to post on social media
stand exactly where you are for hours and wait
payload.explanation: Stewards have radios and lost-people systems for exactly this.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour's gate is open and her elderly dog has wandered into the street where cars are driving past at normal speed during school pickup.
options: stand calmly by the kerb and ask the dog to come gently
chase the dog into the road so cars stop
leave it because the dog knows the street already
wave at every car and tell them to drive faster
payload.explanation: Calm coaxing keeps both you and the dog out of the traffic.

payload.snippet: During a school fire drill your friend wants to sneak back into the classroom to grab her phone because she left it on the desk by accident.
options: tell her drills are practice for real fires and walk out together
wait outside with her stuff while she runs back
go with her so she's not alone in there
tell the teacher loudly so she gets in trouble
payload.explanation: Drills only work when everyone treats them like the real thing.

payload.snippet: Your cousin proudly shows you a homemade rope ladder she's tied to the tree house, and the knots look loose and the rope is fraying near the top.
options: tell her the knots look risky and offer to redo them together
climb it once to test it before saying anything
let her use it and watch in case she falls
cut the rope down without telling her so it's gone
payload.explanation: Honest checks before the climb beat catching her afterwards.

payload.snippet: You're babysitting your little sister and she starts coughing hard at dinner with watery eyes, pointing at her throat and unable to speak properly.
options: stay calm, ask if she's choking, and call an adult straight away
pat her on the back gently and wait for it to pass
give her a big glass of water to wash it down
tell her to stop being dramatic and finish dinner
payload.explanation: Choking signs plus no voice means adult help now, not waiting.

payload.snippet: Your friend's older brother offers to drive you both home from football even though you know he only passed his test last week and has been on his phone.
options: say thanks but you'd rather get the bus as planned
accept because the bus takes ages on a Saturday
go but ask him to put his phone in the glove box
go but sit in the back so it's a bit safer
payload.explanation: Brand new drivers plus phone use is a ride worth skipping.

payload.snippet: Your class is running a paper recycling competition and your friend suggests sneaking extra paper from the staffroom bin to push your tutor group into first place.
options: say no and offer to ask the office for their used paper instead
take the staffroom paper because it's still recycling
tell the teacher your friend cheated and get him disqualified
take only a little so nobody really notices it's gone
payload.explanation: Winning fairly is the point of a class competition.

payload.snippet: At a family party there's only one bin and it's full of takeaway containers, glass bottles and food scraps all mixed together by the end of the night.
options: offer to sort it into the right bins before bed
leave it because it's already too mixed to bother now
tip the whole bag straight into the recycling outside
wait and tell your parents about it tomorrow morning
payload.explanation: Sorting at the end of the night still saves most of it.

payload.snippet: Your school is starting a battery recycling box and your gran has a tin of old batteries she's kept in a drawer for years and wants gone quickly.
options: take them to school in a labelled tub kept upright
throw them in the normal bin because they're really old
post them in the box loose in your school bag
bury them in the garden so they're out of the way
payload.explanation: Old batteries can leak so they need a safe upright trip.

payload.snippet: Your friend laughs when you wash out a yoghurt pot before recycling and says it's a waste of water because the council just sorts everything anyway.
options: rinse it briefly and explain dirty pots get rejected at sorting
stop rinsing because she's probably right about the council
wash it with hot soapy water like a proper dish
throw the pot in the bin so it's not your problem
payload.explanation: A quick rinse is enough and keeps the load recyclable.

payload.snippet: You see a neighbour put bagged garden waste into the general bin every week even though the council provides a free green bin for exactly that.
options: ask politely if she knows the green bin is free to use
report her to the council for breaking the rules
swap her bins around so she has to use the green one
leave it alone because it's none of your business really
payload.explanation: A kind ask works better than swapping or reporting.

payload.snippet: Your family ordered new trainers and the box arrived inside another box inside a plastic mailer, and your dad just chucks the lot in the general bin.
options: fish out the cardboard, flatten it, and put it in recycling
leave it because it's already in the wrong bin now
complain online to the shop about all the packaging
keep the boxes in your room in case they're useful
payload.explanation: Two minutes of fishing out saves a lot of cardboard.

payload.snippet: Your school cafeteria has a food waste caddy but most of your year group still scrape leftovers into the general bin because the caddy looks gross.
options: ask the school council to add clearer signs above the caddy
copy your friends and use the general bin too
tell on each person who uses the wrong bin
scrape your own leftovers but say nothing to anyone
payload.explanation: Better signs change everyone's habit, not just yours.

payload.snippet: Your friend brings a brand new water bottle to every match because she likes a fresh design, and she throws the old one out even when it's barely used.
options: compliment one bottle and suggest sticking with it this term
take her old bottles and use them yourself
lecture her every time she shows up with a new one
post about her habit online so she feels embarrassed
payload.explanation: A friendly nudge lands better than a public lecture.

payload.snippet: Your gran has been saving glass jars for years and her shed is now packed with hundreds she can't possibly use, but she hates throwing things away.
options: help her recycle most and keep a small box for jam-making
throw them all out while she's not looking at home
leave the shed alone because they're her jars not yours
list every jar online for sale without telling her
payload.explanation: Keeping a few honours the habit while clearing the shed.

payload.snippet: Your form room recycling bin is full of crisp packets that can't actually be recycled by the council, and nobody seems to know they're going to landfill anyway.
options: post a small sign and start a separate crisp packet collection
empty the bin into the general one so it's at least correct
tell everyone off for putting crisp packets in there
ignore it because it's the cleaner's job to sort
payload.explanation: A sign plus a separate scheme fixes the cause, not the symptom.

payload.snippet: Your little brother wants to throw away a school jumper he's outgrown, but it's still in decent shape and the school runs a second-hand uniform stall.
options: wash it and drop it off at the school uniform stall on Friday
bin it because second-hand uniforms are a bit cringe
cut it up for cleaning rags around the house
keep it in his wardrobe in case he grows back into it
payload.explanation: Outgrown uniforms still fit someone in the year below.

payload.snippet: Your scout group is doing a litter pick by the river and someone finds a heavy tangle of fishing line with a hook still attached caught in the reeds.
options: tell the leader and let an adult cut it out with gloves
pull it out yourself because nobody else is closer
leave it because it's been there a long time already
snip just the hook off and leave the line behind
payload.explanation: Hooks plus line need adult hands and proper gloves.

payload.snippet: At a birthday party there are paper plates, plastic cups, and metal cans all mixed in one bin bag, and the host's mum is exhausted clearing up alone.
options: offer to help her sort the bag onto the kitchen floor
tie the bag up and put the whole thing in recycling
leave it because it's the host family's job to sort
take photos of the mess and post about it online
payload.explanation: Helping the tired adult is also helping the recycling.

payload.snippet: Your friend's family throws away big food shops every week because they over-buy fresh things and forget about them at the back of the fridge.
options: offer to help her plan a weekly fridge check on Sundays
take the unwanted food home for your own family
tell her parents off for being wasteful at dinner
post about food waste statistics on the family chat
payload.explanation: A simple weekly check stops most of the waste before it starts.

payload.snippet: Your class is doing a clothes swap to cut down on fast fashion and your friend turns up with a bin bag of clothes that are stained, torn, or far too small.
options: thank her, set aside the wearable ones, and send the rest to textile recycling
tell her the whole bag is useless and send it back
put everything on the table and let people sort it themselves
bin the stained ones quietly so she doesn't notice
payload.explanation: Sorting kindly keeps her contribution useful and respected.

payload.snippet: The school vending machine only sells drinks in single-use plastic bottles, and your friend says complaining is pointless because nobody on the council cares.
options: draft a polite letter to the head teacher with a few alternatives
start a loud protest outside the staffroom at lunch
boycott the machine alone and tell nobody about it
keep buying the bottles but recycle them really carefully
payload.explanation: A clear letter with options is harder to ignore than a protest.

payload.snippet: Your aunt gives your family a huge bag of old electronics, including a broken kettle, two phones with cracked screens, and three tangled chargers.
options: take them to the supermarket electronics recycling bank on Saturday
put them in the general bin because they're broken anyway
store them in the loft in case they're worth fixing
post them all online as free even though they don't work
payload.explanation: Electronics recycling banks handle broken kettles and old phones safely.

payload.snippet: Your school librarian wants to throw out forty old paperbacks because they're battered, but you know two charity shops nearby that take used books gladly.
options: offer to bag them up and drop them off this weekend
take the best ones home and let her bin the rest
tell her she's wrong to throw any books away ever
post photos of the binned books online to shame the school
payload.explanation: Charity shops happily take battered paperbacks for resale.

payload.snippet: Your team is doing a beach clean and your friend wants to rush off after twenty minutes because she's bored, even though your section still has loads of plastic.
options: agree to finish your section together then leave on time
let her go and finish the whole section alone yourself
leave with her so you don't have to clean alone
tell the leader she wants to quit early so she's stuck
payload.explanation: Finishing the section together respects the team and the beach.

payload.snippet: Your family bin is overflowing because the truck didn't come this week, and your dad wants to dump the extra bags by the bin shed on the street corner.
options: store them in the garage until next week's collection day
dump them by the shed because everyone else is doing it
leave the extra bags loose by your own bin instead
burn the extra rubbish in the garden after dark
payload.explanation: Storing safely beats fly-tipping, even when the truck skips you.

payload.snippet: You're halfway through a birthday cake for your mum when you realise you've used salt instead of sugar and there's only one egg left in the fridge.
options: start again with the last egg and ask a neighbour for sugar
bake it anyway because she might not notice the salt
give up and buy a cake from the shop instead
add loads of icing on top to hide the salty taste
payload.explanation: Honest restarts make better birthdays than salty surprises.

payload.snippet: Your friend is sleeping over and wants to bake brownies at midnight, but the oven is loud and your little sister has school in the morning.
options: agree to bake them tomorrow morning before breakfast instead
bake them quietly and hope nobody upstairs wakes up
make no-bake brownies on the hob to skip the oven
let her bake alone while you sleep through it
payload.explanation: Midnight ovens aren't worth waking a tired younger sister.

payload.snippet: Your gran is teaching you her famous shortbread but her recipe uses ounces and you only have a digital scale in grams.
options: convert the ounces to grams together and write it on the recipe
guess the amounts and hope it tastes close enough
skip the recipe and use one from the internet instead
use cup measurements you saw on a baking show
payload.explanation: Writing the converted recipe means it works next time too.

payload.snippet: You're baking cookies for a school bake sale when your friend admits she touched the dough after handling her dog without washing her hands.
options: throw the dough out and start again with clean hands
bake it anyway because the oven kills all germs
scoop out the bit she touched and use the rest
sell those cookies and keep the clean ones for home
payload.explanation: Bake sales need a clean batch — your buyers trust the table.

payload.snippet: Your cousin wants to help bake muffins but she keeps eating the chocolate chips, and there won't be enough left to actually put any in the batter.
options: give her a small bowl of chips to eat away from the mixing area
tell her off and send her out of the kitchen completely
let her eat them and use raisins in the muffins instead
lock the chips in a cupboard so she can't reach them
payload.explanation: A small chip bowl keeps her happy and saves the muffins.

payload.snippet: You promised your form tutor a tray of cupcakes for the staff meeting but your oven broke last night and the spare oven is at your gran's house.
options: ask gran if you can bake there straight after school today
turn up empty-handed and apologise on Monday morning
buy supermarket cupcakes and pretend you baked them
make the cupcakes in the microwave instead
payload.explanation: A short bus ride to gran's keeps the promise on time.

payload.snippet: You're baking bread for a charity stall and your friend says white flour is boring and you should add cinnamon, sultanas, and chilli to make it interesting.
options: stick to plain loaves and try her flavours at home another day
add all three because charity buyers love a surprise loaf
add chilli only since it sounds the most exciting flavour
ask your friend to bake her own loaf for the stall
payload.explanation: Charity stalls sell faster when shoppers know what they're buying.

payload.snippet: The cake recipe says fold in the egg whites gently but your little brother is helping and keeps stirring really fast because he thinks faster is better.
options: show him the gentle folding motion slowly and let him try
take the bowl off him and finish it yourself quietly
let him stir fast because it's only a sponge cake
tell him he can never help bake with you again
payload.explanation: Showing the motion teaches him for next time too.

payload.snippet: Your friend's birthday cake needs to be ready by three and the icing is sliding off because the sponge is still warm from the oven at half past two.
options: pop the sponge in the fridge for fifteen minutes to cool
keep adding more icing on top to weigh it down
ice it anyway and hope it firms up by three
give her the cake bare and explain about the icing later
payload.explanation: A quick fridge cool sets the sponge for proper icing.

payload.snippet: You're baking cookies and the recipe says use parchment paper but the kitchen drawer only has tin foil, and your dad is out shopping for another hour.
options: grease a tray well and bake the cookies without paper
use the tin foil because it's basically the same thing
wait an hour for dad to come back with parchment
bake the cookies directly on the oven shelf instead
payload.explanation: A well-greased tray works fine when parchment runs out.

payload.snippet: Your friend says her family recipe is a secret and refuses to share it, but you really want to bake the same biscuits for your school fair next week.
options: ask her to bake them together at hers without writing it down
copy the recipe from a website and pretend it's hers
sulk until she gives in and shares it eventually
tell other people her recipe is probably not that good
payload.explanation: Baking together respects the secret and still gets the biscuits.

payload.snippet: You're trying a new cake recipe online and the comments warn that the cooking time is wrong and the cake burns at the temperature listed.
options: lower the temperature slightly and check it ten minutes early
follow the recipe exactly because the comments might be wrong
ignore the recipe and bake it however you like
skip baking and try a different recipe entirely
payload.explanation: Comment warnings are usually from people who burned the same cake.

payload.snippet: Your mum's birthday cake is in the oven when the smoke alarm goes off because some batter spilled and is burning on the heating element below.
options: open a window and let the cake finish while the smell clears
take the cake out raw to stop the smoke immediately
spray water at the smoke alarm to make it stop beeping
open the oven door and fan the smoke into the room
payload.explanation: Spilled batter burns off quickly with a window open.

payload.snippet: Your sister is allergic to nuts and you're baking brownies, but the only chocolate left in the cupboard has a 'may contain traces of nuts' warning on it.
options: buy a different chocolate from the corner shop first
use it because traces don't really mean any nuts
make the brownies and let her eat a small piece
skip the brownies and make plain biscuits instead
payload.explanation: Trace warnings exist exactly because of sisters like her.

payload.snippet: Your cookies came out flat and crispy when the recipe promised soft and chewy, and your friend at school will be over to try them in twenty minutes.
options: be honest about the mistake and try again with her help
pretend they're meant to be crispy biscuits all along
throw them in the bin and buy some from the shop
hide them and say you forgot to bake any cookies
payload.explanation: Baking together turns a flop into a fun afternoon.

payload.snippet: You're making a celebration cake when your dog jumps up and licks the side of the buttercream just before your aunt arrives to collect it for the party.
options: scrape off the licked side and re-pipe a fresh layer there
smooth it over with a knife and hope nobody notices
give the cake to the dog and apologise to your aunt
deliver it as it is and tell the party afterwards
payload.explanation: Re-piping the licked side keeps the cake safe and presentable.

payload.snippet: Your school baking club has a 'bake from store cupboard only' challenge and your teammate wants to sneak in a packet of fancy chocolate from home.
options: tell her the rules are part of the challenge and use what's there
let her sneak it in because nobody will check
report her to the teacher so she's disqualified now
use her chocolate but pretend it came from the cupboard
payload.explanation: Following the rules makes any win actually feel like a win.

payload.snippet: Your auntie's wedding cake recipe needs three hours of baking but your oven timer broke last week and you keep losing track of how long it's been.
options: set timers on your phone and your dad's phone as backup
guess the time using the kitchen clock and the oven smell
bake it for an extra hour just to be totally safe
skip baking it and ask the bakery for a last-minute cake
payload.explanation: Two phone timers cover you if one phone runs out of battery.

payload.snippet: Your little cousin is helping decorate cupcakes but keeps licking her fingers and putting them back in the sprinkles, and you've still got twelve to do.
options: give her a small bowl of sprinkles that's just for her
let her carry on because they're only family cupcakes
tell her off and send her out of the kitchen
use those sprinkles only on the cupcakes she's keeping
payload.explanation: Her own sprinkle bowl keeps both of you happy and hygienic.

payload.snippet: You're baking bread for your neighbour to thank her for feeding the cat, but you've never made bread before and the dough hasn't risen after an hour.
options: look up why dough doesn't rise and try one more time
bake the flat dough anyway and hope it tastes okay
buy a loaf from the shop and write your name on the bag
skip the gift and just say thanks next time you see her
payload.explanation: Looking up the cause teaches you bread for next time too.

payload.snippet: Your class is planting a sensory garden but your friend keeps treading on the seedlings while messing about, and the seeds were quite expensive for the school to buy.
options: ask her to swap to watering duty so the seedlings stay safe
tell the teacher loudly so she gets in big trouble
let her carry on and replant the squashed seedlings later
do all the planting yourself so she can't ruin it
payload.explanation: Swapping her job protects the seedlings without making a scene.

payload.snippet: Your gran gave you tomato seeds to plant in her greenhouse but you've been so busy with school that they've sat on the kitchen counter for three weeks.
options: plant them this weekend and apologise honestly to gran
throw the seeds away and buy plants from the garden centre
lie and tell her you planted them ages ago already
leave them on the counter for another few weeks
payload.explanation: Honest late planting still gives a summer crop and trust.

payload.snippet: You promised to look after a friend's pot plants while she's on holiday for two weeks, but the heatwave means they need watering twice a day.
options: set a morning and evening reminder on your phone for both
water them every other day and hope they survive
move them all into your bath under the cold tap
give them away because the heatwave is too much trouble
payload.explanation: Two phone reminders match the heatwave's actual watering need.

payload.snippet: Your little brother wants to plant his birthday sunflower seeds in the middle of the lawn where dad mows every Saturday morning without fail.
options: suggest a bright patch by the fence dad never mows
plant them there and put a small flag to warn dad
tell him to wait until he's old enough to choose
plant them in a pot on the patio instead of the ground
payload.explanation: A bright fence patch keeps the sunflowers and dad's routine.

payload.snippet: Your science teacher gave each pupil a bean seed to grow at home but yours hasn't sprouted after two weeks and the project is due on Friday.
options: be honest in the project and explain what might have gone wrong
swap your dead seed with a sprouted one from a friend
buy a bean plant from a shop and pretend it's yours
say the dog ate it so you can't hand anything in
payload.explanation: Honest write-ups about failure still score well in science.

payload.snippet: Your scout group is planting trees on a public verge but the council says you need permission first, and you forgot to send the form in last week.
options: phone the council on Monday and reschedule the planting
plant the trees anyway and ask for forgiveness later
plant them on someone's front garden without asking
give up on the whole tree planting project entirely
payload.explanation: Public planting works when the council actually knows about it.

payload.snippet: Your friend wants to take cuttings from the rose bush in the park because her gran loves roses, but the park sign says not to pick or cut any plants.
options: buy a small rose cutting from the garden centre instead
take a small cutting because nobody is watching now
pick a few rose petals so it counts as less wrong
take cuttings from several bushes so it's spread out
payload.explanation: Park signs apply even when no warden is in sight.

payload.snippet: Your gran's allotment has been neglected since she broke her hip and the weeds are taller than your little cousin who came along to help.
options: agree a small patch to clear together each weekend
try to clear the whole allotment in one Saturday afternoon
give up because the weeds are far too tall now
tell gran to give up the allotment and grow houseplants
payload.explanation: Small weekly patches actually get done and stay done.

payload.snippet: Your form room has a class plant nobody waters because it's nobody's job, and the leaves have started turning yellow and dropping onto your bag.
options: propose a watering rota at the next form meeting on Monday
water it yourself forever so nobody else has to bother
tell the teacher to throw the plant away completely
move the plant to another classroom where it's not yours
payload.explanation: A rota shares the job and the plant actually survives.

payload.snippet: You planted carrot seeds with your little sister but the row is now full of weed seedlings too, and she can't tell the carrots from the weeds at all.
options: show her the carrot leaf shape and weed together slowly
weed it yourself fast so she doesn't pull up carrots
leave the whole row alone and let everything grow
pull up everything and start the seeds again next month
payload.explanation: Teaching her the leaf shape makes her a real gardener.

payload.snippet: Your friend's mum runs a community garden and asks you to help plant strawberries, but you have a maths test on Monday and your last grade was a low one.
options: help for an hour then go home to revise properly
cancel completely and revise the whole weekend instead
go to the garden all day and skip revising entirely
lie to her mum that you have a family thing on
payload.explanation: An hour out and proper revision both fit in one Saturday.

payload.snippet: You watered your tomato plants with cold tap water and now the leaves look limp, and your dad says you should have used water from the rain butt instead.
options: switch to rain butt water from now on and watch them recover
pull up the plants because they're probably ruined now
keep using cold tap water because dad might be wrong
water them with warm tap water instead of cold from now
payload.explanation: Switching the water source usually fixes limp tomato leaves.

payload.snippet: Your school garden club planted bulbs for spring but the autumn term has been so wet the bulbs are starting to rot in the soggy soil before they sprout.

leave them and hope the soil dries out by spring
pull them all out and throw them in the compost bin
buy new bulbs and plant them in exactly the same spot
payload.explanation: Raised beds with grit drain enough to save the bulbs.

payload.snippet: Your friend's dad gave you free packets of seeds but the dates on the back show they expired four years ago, and you're not sure if they'll still grow.
options: plant a few as a test and buy fresh ones if needed
throw the old packets straight in the bin without trying
plant all the seeds and hope half of them work out
ask the dad why he gave you out-of-date seeds
payload.explanation: A small test packet tells you without wasting all the seeds.

payload.snippet: You're planting flowers along the school path but the head teacher walks past and points out you've planted them right where the lawnmower turns each week.
options: move them to the wider verge before the mower returns
leave them and ask the caretaker to mow around them
tell the head teacher you'll move them next term
plant a sign asking the mower to be careful here
payload.explanation: Moving the flowers now is faster than weekly mowing chaos.

payload.snippet: Your cousin sent you cactus seeds from her trip abroad, but customs rules say you can't bring living plant material into the country without a special permit.
options: thank her, tell her the rules, and don't plant the seeds
plant them quietly because nobody at customs will know
give the seeds to a friend in another country to plant
plant just one to see if it grows and bin the rest
payload.explanation: Plant rules protect local nature from foreign pests and diseases.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour's bamboo has spread under the fence and shoots are coming up in your dad's vegetable bed, and he's furious about the damage to his carrots.
options: ask dad to talk calmly to the neighbour about a root barrier
dig up all the bamboo shoots and throw them over the fence
cut the bamboo back without telling the neighbour anything
put cement along the fence line to stop it spreading
payload.explanation: A calm chat about root barriers solves it for both gardens.

payload.snippet: Your sister wants to plant her dead pet hamster in a pot with a seed on top so something living grows out of him, but you're worried it'll attract foxes.
options: suggest burying him in a deep grave with a plant marker on top
agree to the pot because she'll be heartbroken otherwise
tell her dead pets attract foxes and don't help her at all
bury him secretly without her and tell her later
payload.explanation: A deep grave with a plant marker is the kinder, safer version.

payload.snippet: Your community has a no-dig week to protect garden bird nests, but your tulip bulbs were delivered yesterday and the packet says plant in the next three days.
options: store the bulbs cool and dark and plant next week
plant them today because three days is the deadline
plant just half now and the other half next week
leave the bulbs in the shed for the rest of the year
payload.explanation: Cool dark storage keeps bulbs happy past the packet's window.

payload.snippet: Your school plant sale needs ten potted plants from your form by Friday but only three of you actually have anything ready, and people are starting to panic.
options: split cuttings from one big plant to fill the gap quickly
buy seven plants from the shop and label them as homegrown
tell the teacher the form can't make it this year
skip the sale and donate money from your pocket instead
payload.explanation: Cuttings from one healthy plant are honest, free, and quick.

payload.snippet: Your friend's puppy keeps chewing his trainers and his mum says one more pair and the puppy goes back to the rescue centre next weekend.
options: help your friend puppy-proof his room and start basic training
tell him the puppy is just being naughty on purpose
agree the rescue centre would be better for the puppy
buy him cheap trainers so it doesn't matter as much
payload.explanation: Puppy-proofing plus training fixes the cause, not just the trainers.

payload.snippet: Your cat hasn't eaten her breakfast or dinner for two whole days, and she's normally the first one waiting by the bowl every morning without fail.
options: tell your parents tonight and book a vet check tomorrow
wait a few more days to see if her appetite returns
try every food in the cupboard until she eats something
give her treats only and stop offering normal meals
payload.explanation: Two skipped days is the line for a cat — vet it now.

payload.snippet: Your hamster's cage smells really strong because you've been busy with exams, and your mum says it's not your sister's job to clean up after your pet.
options: clean it tonight and set a weekly reminder during exam term
ask your sister to do it just this once as a favour
leave it until exams end in another two weeks
use extra bedding to cover the smell for now
payload.explanation: A weekly reminder protects both the hamster and your sister.

payload.snippet: Your friend keeps feeding her dog chocolate biscuits as treats because the dog loves them, but chocolate is actually toxic for dogs in any amount.
options: tell her kindly about the toxicity and suggest dog-safe treats
report her to her parents so she gets in trouble
wait until the dog gets sick to say something later
let her carry on because the dog seems fine so far
payload.explanation: Telling her now is kinder than waiting for an emergency.

payload.snippet: Your gran's old cat hides under the bed all day now and only comes out at night to eat, even though she used to love sitting on gran's lap.
options: ask gran to book a vet check since hiding is often a pain sign
leave the cat alone because she'll come out when ready
drag the cat out from under the bed for cuddles
tell gran her cat doesn't love her anymore sadly
