dig quickly while she's at lunch and replace the soil neatly
skip the clue and try to guess the final answer without it
tell the teachers their hunt has a bad clue and stop playing
payload.explanation: Permission turns a risky dig into a fun moment with the head.

payload.snippet: Your team's puzzle solution at scout camp is correct but you got it because a different team accidentally shouted theirs across the field at the same time.
options: tell the leader honestly so they can decide what counts
claim the answer because you heard it fair and square
say nothing and hope nobody noticed the shout either
tell the other team they helped you so they get credit too
payload.explanation: Leader's call is the only fair way to handle accidental overhearing.

payload.snippet: Your friend's puzzle game on her tablet has loot boxes that cost real money, and she's been asking her mum's card details to buy the next batch of hint coins.
options: tell her honestly that loot boxes are designed to trap her spending
help her ask her mum so she doesn't have to do it alone
buy a few coins yourself and give them to her as a gift
stop playing her game so you don't have to see it anymore
payload.explanation: Honest words about loot box design help her see it for herself.

payload.snippet: Your family puzzle night was meant to be tonight but your sister has a maths puzzle test tomorrow and is panicking, asking if you can swap puzzle night for next week.
options: swap to next week and help her revise puzzles tonight instead
refuse the swap because puzzle night was planned first
do both — puzzle night and revision at the same table
swap nights but skip helping her revise to keep some fun
payload.explanation: Swapping plus helping turns her test stress into a team night anyway.

payload.snippet: You're doing a magic show at your sister's birthday party and the card trick goes wrong because the wrong card flips out for everyone to see clearly.
options: laugh, own the mistake, and offer to try one more trick
claim you meant to do that and bow proudly anyway
blame the deck and storm off in front of the kids
pretend you didn't see the wrong card flip out
payload.explanation: Owning the mistake keeps the audience on your side.

payload.snippet: Your friend wants to copy the rope trick you learned from your magic kit but she keeps showing the audience the secret during her rehearsal in the playground.
options: show her the hand position that hides the secret first
let her perform it badly so people stop asking her
tell her she's not allowed to copy your tricks at all
video the secret moment and send it to her group chat
payload.explanation: Helping the hand position protects the trick for both of you.

payload.snippet: The school talent show audience includes a kid who saw your coin trick last week and is loudly shouting how it works to everyone around him.
options: smile, swap to a different trick you haven't shown him
argue with him from the stage in front of everyone
do the trick anyway and hope nobody is listening
stop the show and demand he be moved to the back
payload.explanation: A backup trick saves the show without an argument.

payload.snippet: Your magic kit's vanishing scarf trick is missing the special pocket and your cousin's birthday party where you promised to perform is in three hours.
options: swap it for a simpler trick you can do well today
perform it anyway and hope nobody notices the missing pocket
cancel the whole magic show with no warning
buy a new kit from the shop on the way to the party
payload.explanation: A simpler trick done well beats a complicated one fumbled.

payload.snippet: Your friend laughs during your magic show because she saw the trick at her birthday party last month, and now the other kids are starting to lose interest.
options: ask her to be your assistant on the next bigger trick
tell her to leave the room until the show is over
skip ahead to your finale to win them back fast
carry on quietly and ignore the kids who lost interest
payload.explanation: Turning her into the assistant makes the loss of secrecy a win.

payload.snippet: Your little brother breaks your favourite magic prop trying to figure out the trick and lies to your face when you ask what happened to it.
options: show him you know calmly and ask him to help fix it
shout at him until he admits what he broke
go straight to mum and demand he replace your prop
break one of his toys so he learns how it feels
payload.explanation: Calm honesty teaches him better than shouting or revenge.

payload.snippet: You want to do a fire-based magic trick like the magicians on TV, but you're eleven and your parents are at work and your gran is downstairs napping.
options: wait until parents are home and ask them to supervise
try it once quickly in the bathroom over the sink
do it outside in the garden where it's safer
use a candle from the dining room since it's smaller
payload.explanation: Fire tricks need awake adults, full stop.

payload.snippet: Your magic show is meant to last fifteen minutes but you've burned through all your tricks in seven minutes, and parents at the back are checking watches now.
options: do encore versions of your best trick with new volunteers
end the show early and apologise to all the parents
make up a new trick on the spot without practice
ask the audience to give you ten more minutes to plan
payload.explanation: Encore versions stretch time without inventing anything you can't do.

payload.snippet: Your friend wants to be your magician's assistant for the school fete but she's nervous and keeps forgetting her cues during every single rehearsal you do.
options: give her smaller cues with hand signals to make it easier
replace her with someone who actually remembers the cues
do the show alone and not have an assistant after all
shout her cues from the stage so she remembers them
payload.explanation: Smaller hand-signal cues work for nervous assistants on the day.

payload.snippet: The card you palmed has stuck to your sweaty hand and won't drop properly during the reveal, and the audience is staring expectantly while you try to recover.
options: pause, joke about magic being hot work, and try once more
dump all the cards on the floor and walk away from the table
force the card down and reveal the wrong one anyway
blame the audience for sitting too close to the table
payload.explanation: Honest jokes give you a moment to recover the trick.

payload.snippet: Your magic teacher told the class never to reveal tricks, but your little sister keeps crying because she's scared of the disappearing rabbit she just saw at your show.
options: show her the secret quietly so she stops being scared
tell her magic is real and the rabbit is in another world
tell her not to come to your magic shows anymore ever
tell teacher about her crying and ask what to do
payload.explanation: Family fear breaks the rule kindly — secrets aren't worth tears.

payload.snippet: Your show needs a deck of cards but you only have a chess set and three pencils, and your local shop is closed because it's a Sunday afternoon.
options: build a show around mind-reading tricks with the pencils
cancel the show because you don't have any proper cards
use the chess pieces as cards and confuse everyone
borrow cards from a neighbour without asking permission first
payload.explanation: Pencil mind-reading is real magic that needs no cards.

payload.snippet: Your big trick involves a volunteer from the audience but the only kid who volunteered is your friend who already knows exactly how the trick works.
options: thank her and ask for a second volunteer to actually use
use her anyway and hope she pretends to be surprised
skip the trick and do a different one without volunteers
tell the audience there are no volunteers and stop early
payload.explanation: A real surprised volunteer keeps the trick honest and fun.

payload.snippet: Your magic mentor at after-school club catches you using a trick deck for a class show that's meant to be honest tricks only, and other kids notice the deck.
options: own up, swap to honest tricks, and apologise to your class
pretend the trick deck is a normal deck and bluff it out
blame your mentor for not warning you clearly enough
leave the magic club early so you don't get told off
payload.explanation: Owning up and swapping tricks repairs trust with class and mentor.

payload.snippet: Your friend's birthday magic show has to be quiet because her newborn baby brother is asleep, but your best trick involves an audible drumroll and a big shout.
options: swap the drumroll for a finger-snap and a whisper reveal
do it loudly and apologise to her mum if he wakes up
skip the trick because it needs the noise to work
ask her to wake the baby first so noise doesn't matter
payload.explanation: Quiet versions of tricks work and keep babies asleep.

payload.snippet: Your magic show is for ten-year-olds but one of the parents is heckling and trying to expose every trick, ruining the experience for the kids watching.
options: kindly thank her and ask her to enjoy from the back
argue with her in front of all the kids she upset
ignore her and just shout louder than her over the tricks
cancel the show and refuse to perform until she leaves
payload.explanation: Kind redirection protects the kids without ruining the parent's day.

payload.snippet: Your magic prop arrives broken in the post and the show is tomorrow, with no time for a replacement to arrive and your savings already spent on the original.
options: email the seller for a refund and use simpler home tricks
use the broken prop and hope it holds together on stage
cancel the show and disappoint everyone who was coming
ask the seller for an urgent next-day replacement free
payload.explanation: Refund plus home tricks saves the show and the savings.

payload.snippet: You're performing at your gran's care home and one of the residents is shouting out wrong guesses loudly during every trick, distracting all the other watching residents.
options: include her warmly and turn her guesses into part of the show
ask the staff to take her out so others can enjoy
tell her to be quiet so the show can finish properly
skip your remaining tricks and end the show early today
payload.explanation: Including her warmly turns disruption into delight for everyone.

payload.snippet: The magic kit you got for Christmas has a trick where you 'eat' a balloon, but you can't get the secret right and you're choking slightly each time you practise.
options: stop practising the trick and ask online forums for help
keep practising because you'll get the hang of it soon
do the trick at the show without practising enough
swallow the balloon for real to make the trick easier
payload.explanation: Tricks that choke you need expert help before practice continues.

payload.snippet: Your magic show at the fete made twenty pounds for charity, but you also kept five pounds for sweets without telling the school council it came from the takings.
options: give the five back to the council and apologise honestly
keep the money because you did all the work yourself
tell the council you spent it on more magic props instead
give it back without saying why and hope they don't ask
payload.explanation: Honest return restores trust and keeps the charity total true.

payload.snippet: Your gran's train ticket is digital but her phone has died on the platform, and the inspector is already walking down the carriage checking everyone's tickets.
options: show your ticket and explain about gran's dead phone politely
pretend gran isn't with you so she's not asked at all
argue with the inspector that the rules are unfair
hide gran in the toilet until the inspector has moved on
payload.explanation: Polite explanations to inspectors usually get a sensible solution.

payload.snippet: You spot an empty four-seater on a busy commuter train but it has bags on every seat, and the woman in the next row says they're hers and she's holding them.
options: ask politely if she'd mind moving one bag for your gran
sit down and move the bags onto the floor yourself
stand for the whole journey because she said the seats are hers
complain to the train manager about her hogging seats
payload.explanation: A polite ask gives her the chance to do the right thing.

payload.snippet: Your friend pulls the emergency cord on the train as a joke because she wants to see what happens, but the fine is hundreds of pounds if caught.
options: tell the guard honestly when they come and apologise together
pretend it wasn't you when the guard comes round
blame another passenger you don't know for pulling it
swap seats with your friend so the guard asks her
payload.explanation: Honest apology usually beats hiding when the guard arrives.

payload.snippet: Your little brother is bored on the long train journey and starts kicking the seat in front, where a woman is trying to sleep and getting more annoyed.
options: swap seats with him and bring out the colouring book
tell him off loudly so the woman knows you tried
let him carry on because it's a six hour train ride
apologise to the woman but don't change anything yet
payload.explanation: Swapping seats and a colouring book actually stops the kicking.

payload.snippet: Your phone falls down the gap between the train and the platform at a quiet country station, and the next train is in two hours with no staff in sight.
options: press the emergency intercom on the platform for help
lie on the platform and try to reach down for it yourself
wait two hours and try to grab it before the next train
give up and tell mum the phone is lost forever
payload.explanation: Intercoms exist exactly for between-train-and-platform emergencies.

payload.snippet: The man in the seat opposite is loudly arguing on his phone in a way that's clearly upsetting your gran, and the carriage is packed so you can't easily move.
options: ask him politely to take the call to the vestibule
glare at him hard until he notices and stops talking
tell gran to put her headphones in to block him out
record his call on your phone to play back to him
payload.explanation: A polite ask works on most adults in a packed carriage.

payload.snippet: You're travelling alone for the first time and you suddenly realise you got on the wrong train at the previous stop, and you're heading away from your destination.
options: ask the conductor at the next stop how to get back
panic and get off at the very next stop on your own
phone home and cry while staying on the wrong train
stay on hoping the train will turn round eventually
payload.explanation: Conductors know every connection and will get you back.

payload.snippet: Your friend wants to record a TikTok dancing in the train aisle while the train is moving, and other passengers are squeezing past trying to reach the toilet.
options: suggest filming at the station after you both get off
film it anyway because the journey is the best part
film a shorter version so the passengers aren't blocked
stand watch so she gets warned when people are coming
payload.explanation: Station platforms have space and steady ground for dancing videos.

payload.snippet: Your train is delayed an hour and your friend who promised to pick you up at the station is sat in the car park with no phone signal at the other end.
options: find the station free wifi and message her over that
walk home from the station even though it's miles away
wait at the platform and hope she eventually leaves
ask a stranger to lend you their phone for free
payload.explanation: Station wifi reaches the car park and saves everyone waiting.

payload.snippet: You're queuing for the toilet on the train and a much older lady joins behind you looking really uncomfortable, fidgeting and clearly needing it more urgently than you.
options: offer her your place in the queue with a smile
pretend not to notice and use the toilet first yourself
ask everyone in front to let her skip the whole queue
stand aside and wait for everyone after her to go too
payload.explanation: Offering your place is the small kind thing on a long journey.

payload.snippet: Your seat reservation is on a train that's been cancelled and the next train is rammed, but your reserved seat number on the new train has another passenger sleeping in it.
options: show your reservation to the guard and let them sort it
wake the sleeping passenger and demand your seat back
stand for the whole journey because the train is rammed
take any free seat and complain online about it later
payload.explanation: Guards handle reservation clashes — that's literally their job.

payload.snippet: Your group of school friends are messing around on the platform and one of them is leaning over the edge to see how close the train comes, with the train one minute away.
options: pull her gently back and tell her how close the train is
tell her to lean further so it makes a better TikTok
tell the platform staff before the train arrives now
wait until the train comes and laugh about it later
payload.explanation: Pulling her back gently saves a TikTok from becoming a tragedy.

payload.snippet: Your gran left her handbag on the train when you got off, and inside is her glasses, her purse, and the only photo she has of grandad as a young man.
options: tell station staff right now and give them gran's details
wait until you get home and phone lost property tomorrow
buy gran a new bag with similar bits to replace it
blame gran for not paying enough attention to her bag
payload.explanation: Station staff radio ahead and often catch bags at the next stop.

payload.snippet: Your friend who has hayfever is sneezing constantly on the train and the woman across the aisle keeps making loud unkind comments about catching her germs.
options: calmly tell the woman it's hayfever and offer your friend tissues
argue loudly with the woman about being prejudiced about sneezing
swap seats so your friend is further from the woman
ignore it and pretend you can't hear the woman's comments
payload.explanation: Calm facts about hayfever shut down unkind comments without a fight.

payload.snippet: You see someone slip a phone out of the bag of a sleeping passenger sitting two rows ahead, and they're now putting the phone into their own pocket quietly.
options: press the call button discreetly and wait for the guard
shout 'thief' loudly across the whole train carriage
tackle the person yourself to get the phone back fast
wake the sleeping passenger and tell them what happened
payload.explanation: Call buttons get the guard there safely without confrontation.

payload.snippet: Your scout group is taking up six seats in priority seating and an elderly man with a stick has just got on at a stop with no other free seats left.
options: stand up and offer him a priority seat with the others
pretend not to see him and hope he asks someone else
leave only one priority seat free and keep the rest
ask the leader if you have to give up your seats
payload.explanation: Priority seats exist for exactly this man's situation right now.

payload.snippet: Your phone shows the train is replacing the rail line with a bus, but your gran isn't great with buses and the rail staff can't tell you exactly when it'll arrive.
options: ask staff to arrange assisted travel for gran on the bus
leave gran at the station and complete the journey alone
wait for any later train rather than using the bus
tell gran she'll have to manage the bus alone today
payload.explanation: Assisted travel makes the bus possible and gran feel safer.

payload.snippet: Your seat is by an open window and the wind is freezing the gran in the seat behind, but the man next to you says he's hot and wants the window open further.
options: suggest closing it slightly and ask the guard about temperature
close the window and let the man complain to the guard
leave it open because grandma will warm up eventually
tell gran to swap seats with you for the rest of the journey
payload.explanation: A small compromise plus guard input solves both temperatures.

payload.snippet: You're alone on a quiet late train and a passenger starts asking you personal questions and which station you're getting off at, making you really uncomfortable.
options: move to the carriage with the guard and stay there
answer the questions politely so they leave you alone
lie about your station so they get off at the wrong place
shout at them loudly so other passengers hear you
payload.explanation: The guard's carriage has staff and CCTV and stops the questions.

payload.snippet: Your train booking is the cheap advance ticket only valid on the named train, but you missed that train and the staff at the gate are checking everyone's tickets carefully.
options: explain honestly at the gate and ask to buy an upgrade
walk through the barrier when nobody is looking carefully
argue with the staff that the advance rule is unfair now
wait at the station until the original train tomorrow
payload.explanation: Honest upgrades at the gate are cheaper than fines on the next train.

payload.snippet: Your little brother runs off down the beach chasing a seagull and disappears behind a row of beach huts, and your mum has just nipped to the loo.
options: stay where you are and ring mum so she joins the search
chase him alone and leave your bags on the sand
ask a random adult to look after him until mum returns
shout for him once and assume he'll come back soon
payload.explanation: Staying put and calling mum keeps two of you findable, not lost.

payload.snippet: The tide is coming in fast and you and your friend have built a brilliant sandcastle close to the water, but it's also where your cousin's bag is sitting.
options: grab the bag first then watch the sandcastle from higher up
save the sandcastle and leave the bag for last
let the sea take both because tides aren't a real emergency
carry the bag and the sandcastle together to higher ground
payload.explanation: Bags before sandcastles — phones and keys don't survive seawater.

payload.snippet: You spot a beach warning flag that's red and the lifeguard has just stopped a family from going in, but your friend insists the waves still look fine to her.
options: trust the lifeguard and swim another day this week
go in anyway because she's a strong swimmer and confident
go in only up to your knees because that's safe enough
argue with the lifeguard that the flag is wrong today
payload.explanation: Red flags exist for things you can't see from the sand.

payload.snippet: Your sister is using a brand new inflatable lilo at sea and the wind is starting to blow her further from the shore than you can comfortably swim out to.
options: call her in now and tell the lifeguard if she won't
swim out yourself and bring her back in alone
shout from the beach and hope she hears you
go on your own lilo so you both drift together
payload.explanation: Lifeguards have boards and can reach drifting lilos fast.

payload.snippet: Your cousin steps on a piece of broken glass while paddling, and her foot is bleeding through her sock, and the nearest first aid is at the pier ten minutes away.
options: wrap a clean towel tightly and walk her slowly to first aid
let her run to first aid so it bleeds less time
wash the cut in salty seawater so it heals fast
wait on the beach to see if the bleeding stops first
payload.explanation: Pressure with a clean towel works while you walk to help.

payload.snippet: Your friend wants to bury her brother up to the neck in sand for a TikTok, but the tide is due in twenty minutes and he's already laughing too hard to argue.
options: bury him in legs only and film that version instead
bury him fully but dig him out fast before the tide
do the full burial since twenty minutes is loads
let him bury her instead to swap the risk
payload.explanation: Legs-only is still funny and still safely fast to undig.

payload.snippet: Your sandwiches are still on the towel and a seagull the size of a small dog is approaching with a really interested look on its face right now.
options: put the food in the cool bag and zip it shut
wave your arms at the bird and shout very loudly
throw one sandwich at it so it leaves the rest
let it eat them and buy more from the kiosk
payload.explanation: Zipped cool bags beat seagulls every single time.

payload.snippet: Your gran's parasol blows over and is rolling across the beach towards a family with a sleeping baby and a half-eaten picnic spread out around them.
options: chase it down quickly and apologise before it reaches them
let them stop it because they're closer to it
shout a warning and let it land where it lands
stand and watch in case it stops on its own
payload.explanation: Chasing it now is better than waking a sleeping baby.

payload.snippet: You forgot suncream and the beach kiosk has run out, and it's a thirty-degree day with no shade except for a small bit under the pier far down the beach.
options: ask other families if they can spare some suncream
stay out in full sun and hope you don't burn
sit under the pier for the entire day in the shade
go home now and skip the rest of the beach day
payload.explanation: Most beach families pack extra suncream and share gladly.

payload.snippet: Your friend says she can hear someone yelling 'help' from the rocks at the edge of the cove, but the rocks are slippery and you've never climbed them before.
options: tell the lifeguard immediately and don't go on the rocks
climb the rocks together to see who's calling
shout back from the beach and hope they reply
ignore it because it might just be kids messing about
payload.explanation: Lifeguards have ropes and training for rock rescues.

payload.snippet: Your friend's body board snapped a fin on a sharp rock and she wants to go back in the sea anyway, even though a broken fin can scratch her badly while paddling.
options: swap with her broken board and use yours yourself instead
let her use the broken board because she really wants to
tell her she has to sit out for the rest of the day
snap your fin too so you both have the same problem
payload.explanation: Swapping boards keeps the broken fin away from her legs.

payload.snippet: Your dad fell asleep on the lounger and his back is bright red already, and you can see the lobster colour spreading even while you're standing watching him.
options: wake him gently and bring the parasol over right now
leave him because he'll wake up when he's ready
pour cold water on his back to cool the burn fast
tell mum and let her decide whether to wake him
payload.explanation: Stopping the burn now beats hours of aloe vera later.

payload.snippet: You found a jellyfish on the sand and your little sister wants to poke it with a stick to see if it moves, but some jellyfish still sting after they're washed up.
options: tell her not to touch it and call the lifeguard about it
let her poke it gently with a really long stick
kick sand over it so nobody else gets stung either
pick it up with your towel and throw it back in
payload.explanation: Beached jellyfish sting for hours after they look dead.

payload.snippet: Your phone is in your shorts pocket and you've just walked straight into the sea up to your waist without thinking, and the screen is now showing a black water-damage warning.
options: switch it off, dry it gently, and tell your parents honestly
plug it into a charger when you get back home tonight
shake it really hard to get the water back out
put it in a bowl of rice for the next three days
payload.explanation: Off and dry is the first step; honesty buys repair help.

payload.snippet: Your school's beach clean group finds a tangled mess of fishing net with a dead crab and a tatty plastic six-pack ring, and your friend wants to wear the net as a cape.
options: bag it carefully and bin it as proper hazardous waste
take it home to use as decoration in your bedroom
put it back in the sea because that's where it came from
wear it briefly because the crab is already dead
payload.explanation: Hazardous bins exist for tangles that hurt other wildlife next.

payload.snippet: The beach toilets are gross and your little brother is desperate but refuses to go in there, and the next public toilets are a twenty minute walk away.
options: go with him and reassure him so he uses the smelly one
let him wee in the sea since everyone does that
make him hold it until you walk to the next ones
let him go behind the beach huts where it's private
payload.explanation: Going with him gets a smelly job done in two minutes.

payload.snippet: You see a kid you don't know struggling in the shallow water and his older brother is on his phone twenty metres up the beach not paying any attention to him.
options: shout to the lifeguard and run to tell the brother
wade in and pull the kid out by yourself quickly
wait to see if the kid figures it out himself
tell your mum and let her decide what to do
payload.explanation: Shouting brings the trained rescuer while you fetch family.

payload.snippet: The wind has picked up and your beach windbreak keeps blowing over, and twice now the wooden poles have nearly hit a family sat behind you on the sand.
options: take the windbreak down and pack it away safely
keep trying to stake it deeper into the wet sand
ask the family to move further down the beach
tie it to a deckchair so the wind can't catch it
payload.explanation: Falling poles aren't worth the wind protection on a windy day.

payload.snippet: Your friend dropped her engagement-style holiday bracelet in the rockpool and it's just out of reach behind a clump of seaweed, with the tide rising minute by minute.
options: grab a stick from the beach and fish it out quickly
wait until low tide tomorrow and check the pool again
ask the lifeguard to wade in and grab it for you
leave it and tell her it was probably never that important
payload.explanation: A stick fishing rod works in seconds before the tide wins.

payload.snippet: Your mum left her purse on the picnic blanket while she's in the sea with your sister, and a group of teenagers are now sitting suspiciously close to your stuff.
options: sit on the blanket yourself until mum gets back out
take the purse into the sea inside a plastic bag
ask the lifeguard to come and watch your stuff
leave it and trust that nobody would actually take it
payload.explanation: Sitting on the blanket is the cheapest, quickest deterrent.

payload.snippet: School is closed for snow and your friend wants to sledge down the hill that ends near the main road, even though the road is still busy with slow-moving traffic.
options: suggest sledging on the smaller hill in the park instead
go to the main-road hill but stop yourselves with feet
go and just sledge halfway down to be safer
go but film each other in case anyone falls badly
payload.explanation: Park hills don't end in traffic when the snow is heavy.

payload.snippet: Your gran needs her shopping but the pavements are sheets of ice, and she's been trying to call a taxi for an hour with no luck on the snow day.
options: offer to walk to the shop with her shopping list
tell her to wait until tomorrow when the ice melts
carry her bags but let her walk on the ice herself
drag a sledge behind you and pull gran the whole way
payload.explanation: Walking with her list saves her the icy trip entirely.

payload.snippet: Your snowman is the best you've ever built but the kids next door want to knock it down for a video, and they keep ringing the doorbell asking if they can.
options: say no firmly and explain you'd be upset if they did
let them so they leave you alone for the rest of the day
ignore the doorbell and hope they get bored eventually
build them a second snowman they're allowed to knock down
payload.explanation: Saying no firmly teaches them to ask properly next time.

payload.snippet: Your little sister has been outside in the snow for two hours and her gloves are soaked through, but she's begging to stay out because all her friends are still playing.
options: swap her gloves for dry ones and set a thirty-minute timer
let her stay because she says her hands aren't cold
drag her inside crying so she doesn't get frostbite
tell her one minute warning and then bring her in
payload.explanation: Dry gloves plus a timer is the kind way to keep her safe.

payload.snippet: Your dad's car is stuck in snow at the bottom of the drive and he's getting frustrated trying to push it alone, and your scout group has a tow rope in the garage.
options: fetch the tow rope and offer to help him push together
stay inside because he didn't ask for your help yet
video him struggling and post it for a laugh later
tell him to give up and walk to work instead
payload.explanation: Bringing the rope and helping is what dads remember.

payload.snippet: Your friend slips on ice walking to your house and you hear a crack as her arm hits the wall, and she's now sat on the kerb white-faced refusing to move at all.
options: ring her parents and 111 and stay sitting with her
help her up and walk her to your house slowly
tell her to wait there while you run for help
ignore her because she's probably just being dramatic
payload.explanation: White-faced after a crack means stay still and call for help.

payload.snippet: Your snowball fight with the neighbours has turned mean and the boy across the road keeps putting ice in his snowballs to make them hurt the smaller kids playing.
options: stop the game and tell him ice snowballs end it now
start putting ice in yours too so it's fair to him
tell the smaller kids to go inside and play another day
throw a really hard one at him to teach him a lesson
payload.explanation: Ending the game with a clear rule protects the smaller kids.

payload.snippet: Your school is closed but your maths teacher posted homework on the class page, and your friends are saying it's optional because the school is officially shut today.
options: do the homework because she clearly meant it to be done
skip it because the school is closed officially today
do half so you can say you tried at least
wait until tomorrow and copy off your friends quickly
payload.explanation: Posted homework on a snow day still counts when school's back.

payload.snippet: Your gran's heating broke overnight and her flat is freezing, and the engineer can't come until tomorrow because of snow on all the roads.
options: bring hot water bottles, blankets, and ask mum to invite her round
leave her alone since the engineer is coming tomorrow
lend her your portable fan heater for tonight only
tell her to wear extra layers and she'll be okay
payload.explanation: Bringing comforts and inviting her round beats waiting and freezing.

payload.snippet: Your friend wants to build an ice slide on the path outside your house, even though postal workers and the dog walker use that path every single morning.
options: build the slide in your garden instead of on the path
build it on the path and put up a warning sign
build it but break it up at the end of every day
build it really small so it's not too dangerous
payload.explanation: Garden slides don't risk strangers' ankles on the morning round.

payload.snippet: You promised to walk a neighbour's dog while she's at work, and the snow is now too deep for the dog's short legs to manage the usual route across the field.
options: do a shorter loop around the cleared pavements instead
skip the walk and apologise to her when she's home
carry the dog through the deep snow on your shoulders
do the usual route and drag him through the deep bits
payload.explanation: Cleared pavements still count as a walk and protect his legs.

payload.snippet: Your friends are throwing snowballs at cars driving past the park, and one driver has just pulled over looking really angry about a snowball hitting his windscreen.
options: apologise honestly and stop throwing at any more cars
run away before the angry driver gets out properly
tell him your friends did it and not actually you
throw another snowball to show you're not scared
payload.explanation: Apologising defuses the driver and stops the dangerous game.

payload.snippet: Your school bus is cancelled and your mum can't drive in snow, but you've got a piano exam in town that you've been working towards for the last six months.
options: ring the exam centre and ask about rescheduling today
walk the eight miles into town through the snow alone
skip the exam and lose the chance and the money
ask a friend's dad with a four-wheel drive for a lift
payload.explanation: Exam centres reschedule for snow because everyone is in the same boat.

payload.snippet: Your friend doesn't own snow boots and her trainers are soaked already, but she still wants to spend all day out building snow forts with the group in the park.
options: lend her your spare welly boots and warm dry socks
tell her to go home because her feet will get cold
let her carry on because she said her feet are fine
stay inside with her so she doesn't have to walk back
payload.explanation: Spare boots are why scout-mums keep two pairs in the cupboard.

payload.snippet: Your snow day means you've got six hours free, and your friend wants you both to game online all day, but your mum asked you to clear the front path before noon.
options: clear the path quickly then game with your friend afterwards
skip the path because mum will probably forget about it
ask your friend to help you clear it then game faster
game all day and clear the path quickly before mum returns
payload.explanation: Clearing first means guilt-free gaming and a happy mum at noon.

payload.snippet: Your cat slipped out the front door in the snow and is sitting on the wall across the road, refusing to come back even though the snow is settling on her fur.
options: open a tin of tuna by the door and call her gently
walk into the road to fetch her despite the snow tyres
leave her because cats always come home when ready
throw a snowball near her so she runs back inside
payload.explanation: Tuna tin works faster than any chasing in snow.

payload.snippet: Your sister is sledging at the park and her sledge tipped over near the bottom of the hill, and an older kid has now taken her sledge and won't give it back.
options: go over together and ask calmly for the sledge back
tell on him to his parents who are watching from the top
wrestle him for the sledge and bring it back quickly
tell sister to share because there's plenty of snow
payload.explanation: Calm joint ask works on most older kids without a fight.

payload.snippet: Your friend wants to make snow angels on the field but the snow there is thin and patchy with mud underneath, and she's wearing her brand-new white coat from her gran.
options: suggest the deeper snow on the playground instead
let her do it in mud because the coat will wash out
tell her to take the coat off before lying down
do snow angels yourself and let her watch instead
payload.explanation: Deeper snow protects gran's gift and still makes great angels.

payload.snippet: Your friend's family lost power overnight and her phone is dead, and she walked through deep snow to your house to ask if she can stay warm with you for the day.
options: of course let her in and ring her parents from yours
text her parents first to check it's okay with them
say yes but only until her power comes back on
say no because mum hasn't agreed to a visitor today
payload.explanation: Of course is the right answer; the call to parents follows.

payload.snippet: Your snow day video idea needs you to jump off the garden shed roof into a deep snow drift, and your friend has filmed himself doing the same thing yesterday already.
options: skip the jump and film an epic snowball fight instead
do the jump because his video shows it's totally safe
do a smaller jump from the picnic bench to be safer
jump but land sitting down so it doesn't hurt your legs
payload.explanation: Snow looks soft but hides bricks, slabs, and broken bones.

payload.snippet: Your group's volcano experiment for the science fair tipped over and dyed the head teacher's white tablecloth bright red, and judging starts in twenty minutes.
options: apologise honestly and offer to wash it before judging
hide the stain by covering it with our display board
blame the head teacher for putting a white cloth out
pour more red liquid so the whole cloth looks the same
payload.explanation: Honest cleanup gets respect and saves the experiment's reputation.

payload.snippet: Your friend wants to mix bleach and vinegar in your science club beaker to see what happens, even though the back of the bottle warns about toxic gas.
options: stop her and explain the toxic gas warning on the label
let her mix a tiny amount so she sees it isn't dramatic
mix it together so you can both write up the results
report her to the teacher without saying anything first
payload.explanation: Bleach plus vinegar is real chlorine gas — not a maybe.

payload.snippet: Your egg drop experiment is due in tomorrow and your design works perfectly, but your friend's design failed twice and she's asking to copy yours overnight.
options: help her redesign hers tonight so she learns the principles
lend her your design because friends help each other
tell her tough luck and her grade is her own problem
make a slightly different version for her to hand in
payload.explanation: Teaching her the principle saves her grade and the friendship.

payload.snippet: You're growing mould on bread for a biology project and the smell has filled your bedroom, and your little brother has started sneezing and his eyes look puffy now.
options: move the experiment to the garden shed tonight
leave it because the project needs another three days
throw the bread away and start the experiment again later
open the window and hope his eyes settle down on their own
payload.explanation: Puffy eyes plus sneezing means moving the mould, not waiting.

payload.snippet: Your teacher said you can test acidity at home but the only liquids in your kitchen are cleaning products under the sink with skull-and-crossbones warning symbols.
options: swap to lemon juice and vinegar for the test instead
use a tiny amount of the cleaning product carefully
skip the experiment because home has nothing usable
use the cleaning product but wear washing-up gloves first
payload.explanation: Skull symbols mean kitchen ingredients only, always.

payload.snippet: Your science fair project measures heart rates and your friend wants to use her gran as a test subject, but her gran has a heart condition and is on medication for it.
options: test other family members and write up that ethical choice
test gran but ask her to lie about feeling any pain
test gran briefly because one test won't really matter
skip the experiment and choose a different project entirely
payload.explanation: Ethical exclusions show good science, not weakness in a project.

payload.snippet: Your volcano made too much foam and it's now overflowing onto your dad's brand new laptop that you weren't allowed to be near, and the foam is touching the keyboard.
options: lift the laptop and tell dad straight away after
wipe the foam off quickly and don't tell dad at all
blame your sister so dad doesn't get angry with you
carry on with the experiment and hope the laptop survives
payload.explanation: Lifting first, telling second saves the laptop and trust.

payload.snippet: Your friend wants to test if a microwave really blows up grapes, but you both know your mum's microwave is the only one in the house and replacements cost a lot.
options: watch the experiment on YouTube together instead
do it once quickly and hope the microwave still works
do it in your gran's microwave so mum's stays safe
skip the microwave step but write up the results anyway
payload.explanation: YouTube shows the result without risking the family microwave.

payload.snippet: Your school's science club wants you to test a heavy chemistry kit at home over half term, but your house has two cats who get into absolutely everything left on counters.
options: ask the teacher if you can do the kit at school instead
take it home and shut the kitchen door very carefully
take it home and leave it on top of the wardrobe
swap kits with a friend who doesn't have any pets
payload.explanation: School chemistry stays safer at school when curious cats live home.

payload.snippet: You spilled iron filings all over your gran's living room carpet during your magnet experiment, and her vacuum is broken until the engineer comes on Friday.
options: use a magnet wrapped in a plastic bag to lift them all out
leave the filings until Friday when the vacuum is fixed
rub them deep into the carpet so they vanish from sight
blame your little brother and run upstairs to your room
payload.explanation: Magnets through plastic lift filings cleanly in five minutes.

payload.snippet: Your friend claims her science project results match the textbook prediction perfectly, but you saw her make up the numbers because the real experiment didn't work first time.
options: encourage her to repeat the test honestly and write what happened
tell the teacher straight away that she made up data
ignore it because her project isn't really your problem
copy her made-up method so both of you can match the textbook
payload.explanation: Repeating honestly gives her a real chance to fix it before marking.

payload.snippet: Your dry ice experiment is creating spectacular fog but your asthmatic little sister came into the kitchen and is starting to cough hard from breathing the carbon dioxide.
options: stop the experiment and open the back door immediately
finish the experiment quickly while she watches in the doorway
tell her to go back upstairs and shut the kitchen door
carry on but ask her to use her inhaler beforehand just in case
payload.explanation: Asthma plus dry ice is stop now, not finish first.

payload.snippet: Your group experiment for the school fair needs four people but two of you have been doing all the work, and the other two want their names on the final display board.
options: ask the lazy two for a clearly listed final contribution
put all four names on because they're still in the group
leave them off the board so they get a grade penalty
do their part for them so the project doesn't fail completely
payload.explanation: Listed contributions are fair to the workers and the fair.

payload.snippet: You're testing plant growth under different lights and your gran has been moving the pots to her sunny windowsill when nobody's looking, ruining the experiment design.
options: explain kindly why she shouldn't move them and label each pot
tell mum so she stops gran from going near them again
start the experiment again and lock the pots in your room
let gran carry on because her windowsill is doing them good
payload.explanation: A kind explanation plus labels stops the move and saves the project.

payload.snippet: Your class is doing electric circuit experiments and your friend wants to connect a battery to the metal pencil sharpener, even though the teacher said batteries to bulbs only.
options: stop her and remind her about the bulbs-only rule
let her try because the battery is only nine volts
video her doing it so the teacher sees afterwards
join in but only after she's done it first safely
payload.explanation: Class rules in science exist because of melted sharpeners.

payload.snippet: Your homemade rocket experiment in the garden landed in your neighbour's pond and his pet koi carp are now swimming around the plastic fins poking out of the water.
options: knock on his door and ask to fish out the rocket carefully
leave the rocket and hope he doesn't notice ever
wait until his car leaves and grab it over the fence
tell him your sister threw the rocket in by accident
payload.explanation: Knocking now protects the koi and your neighbour's trust forever.

payload.snippet: Your friend's bicarb-and-vinegar erupting cake is amazing but it's covering your dad's good clock on the kitchen counter, and the lid is starting to fizz onto the clock face.
options: move the clock to safety and pause the experiment now
let it carry on because it's the best bit of the experiment
wipe the clock face quickly without stopping the cake
video the clock fizzing because it'll look really good
payload.explanation: Pausing for two seconds saves a clock dad actually loves.

payload.snippet: You found out your science project graph would look better if you slightly bent one data point, and your friend says nobody at the school fair will ever check your maths.
options: leave the data honest and show what really happened
bend the point because the rest of the project is accurate
redo the experiment until you get the result you want
remove the bad point and say you only ran four tests
payload.explanation: Honest graphs win the fair and teach you real science.

payload.snippet: Your sister wants to try your slime experiment but the borax in the recipe says not for kids under five, and she's only three but she's promising to wash her hands afterwards.
options: make a borax-free version using flour and water instead
let her help because she promised about her hands
let her watch you make it but not touch any of it
tell her no and refuse to let her watch the experiment
payload.explanation: Flour-and-water slime is safe at three and just as gooey.

payload.snippet: Your school science club is testing food samples for sugar but one tester wants to test medicine from her bag, and the teacher just stepped out to take a phone call.
options: say no firmly and wait for the teacher to come back
let her test it because medicine is basically just chemicals
test it together so you can both check the result
tell the teacher about it when she eventually returns
payload.explanation: Medicine isn't a science club sample without the teacher there.

payload.snippet: Your class is feeding the goats and your friend keeps trying to grab the goat's beard for a photo, even though the farmer warned everyone not to grab any of the animals.
options: remind her of the farmer's rule and offer to take her photo posed
let her do it because the goat seems pretty calm today
tell the farmer straight away so she gets told off
grab the beard yourself so the goat gets used to it
payload.explanation: Posed photos beat grabbed beards every single time.

payload.snippet: Your little brother wanders off into the pig enclosure when nobody is looking, and the boar at the back is huge and your dad is busy at the gift shop counter.
options: call the farmer to safely get your brother out now
climb in yourself and grab him before the boar moves
shout at him from outside the fence to come back
wait at the gate hoping he comes out on his own
payload.explanation: Farmers know the boar; you and your brother do not.

payload.snippet: Your gran's mobility scooter battery dies halfway round the farm walk, and the visitor centre is on the other side of the duck pond up a long hill.
options: tell the farm staff so they can collect gran with a buggy
push gran up the hill yourselves even though it's heavy
leave gran sat by the duck pond while you walk for help
tell gran she has to walk the rest of the way slowly
payload.explanation: Farm staff have buggies for exactly this kind of mobility problem.

payload.snippet: Your friend wants to feed the horse some of her packed lunch crisps, but the sign clearly says only farm-approved food because human snacks make horses ill quickly.
options: show her the sign and offer her the farm feed instead
let her feed one because one crisp won't really matter
feed the horse together so you both get told off equally
tell the farmer she's about to feed the horse crisps
payload.explanation: Signs about animal food are written from actual vet bills.

payload.snippet: Your school trip is at the farm and someone in your class has a phobia of geese, and the geese have just been let out into the visitor area where everyone is walking.
options: walk with her and ask staff for a different route round the geese
tell her she has to face her fear sometime in life
leave her behind and meet her at the gift shop later
shoo the geese away yourself so she can walk through
payload.explanation: Walking with her and asking staff respects the phobia properly.

payload.snippet: Your dad parked the car in a muddy field and the wheels are now stuck deep in the mud, and the queue of cars behind yours is starting to honk and complain loudly.
options: tell dad to ask the farmer for the tractor right now
push the car yourself from behind so it gets out faster
tell the honkers to be quiet because dad is trying his best
wait in the car and let dad sort the mud out alone
payload.explanation: Tractors live on farms exactly for this kind of mud situation.

payload.snippet: Your cousin slips on cow poo in the milking parlour and lands in it face down, and she's now crying because her brand new white coat from gran is completely ruined.
options: comfort her, wash the coat in the farm tap, and reassure her
laugh because it's actually quite funny when you think about it
tell her gran will buy her a new coat after the holiday
video the moment to show the family back home later
payload.explanation: Comfort plus a tap-wash matters more than the coat right now.

payload.snippet: Your friend wants to climb the hay bale stack at the back of the barn for a photo, but the farmer specifically said the bales aren't stable and could collapse any minute.
options: say no and suggest a photo with the calves instead
climb just a little bit to one bale rather than the top
stand at the bottom while she climbs to the top alone
video her climbing in case the bales actually do collapse
payload.explanation: Calves make better photos than hospital visits from a bale collapse.

payload.snippet: Your gran wants to bottle-feed the lamb but her hands are shaky and the lamb is hungry and tugging hard, and the bottle keeps slipping out of her grip onto the floor.
options: kneel beside gran and hold the bottle with her together
take over so the lamb gets fed faster without the slipping
let gran carry on alone because she really wants to do it
tell the farmer that gran can't manage the feeding properly
payload.explanation: Holding together gives gran the moment and the lamb the milk.

payload.snippet: Your phone's charging point at the visitor centre is in use and yours is on three percent, but your dad expects you to check in by text when the school trip is over.
options: ask the visitor centre staff if there's a charging spare
use your friend's phone to text dad from her account
tell dad afterwards and apologise for not checking in
wait at the charger until the other phone is finished
payload.explanation: Staff often have a spare cable behind the counter.

payload.snippet: Your group's farm scavenger hunt clue says find the hen with three black feathers, and your friend wants to dye one of the brown hens to match so you can win quickly.
options: carry on looking honestly and tell her dye on hens is unkind
dye the hen because it's just one harmless small win
ask the farmer if any hen has black feathers anywhere
give up and just submit any random hen for the answer
payload.explanation: Honest searching protects hens and earns a real win.

payload.snippet: You see a kid from another school throwing stones at the sheep in the field, and the sheep are running confused in circles every time another stone lands near them.
options: tell a farm staff member immediately with what you saw
shout at the kid yourself across the path very loudly
throw a stone at the kid to teach him a hard lesson
ignore it because his teachers should be watching him properly
payload.explanation: Staff intervene fast — sheep stress matters and gets recorded.

payload.snippet: The farm shop has free apple samples and your friend is on her sixth sample, and the lady running the stall is starting to give your friend really pointed looks.
options: tell your friend kindly that one or two samples is the norm
take a few more yourself so the lady stares at you instead
ignore it because samples are free for everyone to try
buy something small from the stall to make up for it
payload.explanation: A kind word now prevents the lady having to say something.

payload.snippet: Your wellies are leaking and your feet are freezing after walking through the duck pond field, and the farm visit still has another two hours of outdoor activities planned.
options: ask the gift shop if they sell or lend dry socks
carry on because complaining will spoil it for everyone else
sit out the rest of the visit in the visitor centre cafe
swap wellies with your dad even though his are much bigger
payload.explanation: Gift shops often have emergency socks for exactly leaky wellies.

payload.snippet: Your friend's nose is running from hay fever and she's wiping it on her hand before petting the rabbits, and the next family in the queue has a baby in their arms.
options: offer her a tissue and gentle hand sanitiser before she touches rabbits
let her pet the rabbits because rabbits don't catch human colds
tell her to wash her hands when she's finished petting them
warn the next family quietly so they know to wait
payload.explanation: Tissue plus sanitiser protects rabbits and the baby behind her.

payload.snippet: You drop your school worksheet into the pig pen and the pigs are starting to chew it up, but the worksheet has all the answers you spent the morning writing on.
options: ask the farmer for a fresh worksheet and copy your memory back
climb into the pig pen to grab it back before it's eaten
tell the teacher the pigs ate the worksheet so it's gone
wait until the pigs finish eating and pick up the bits left
payload.explanation: Farmers carry spares and memory beats climbing in with pigs.

payload.snippet: Your gran is asking the farmer too many detailed questions about cattle disease, and the queue behind you is growing impatient and a parent has now started tutting loudly.
options: thank the farmer politely and offer to walk gran round again later
interrupt gran and pull her away from the farmer immediately
ignore the tutting because gran is genuinely interested
turn to the parent and tell them to be more patient
payload.explanation: Thanks plus a later return respects gran and the queue.

payload.snippet: Your friend tries to ride the donkey when no one's looking even though the sign says no riding, and the donkey is starting to shift uncomfortably under her weight.
options: tell her to get off now and apologise to the donkey staff
let her finish a quick lap because the donkey can take it
stand watch so a staff member doesn't see her riding
ride a different animal yourself so you're both in trouble
payload.explanation: Donkey signs come from years of donkey back injuries.

payload.snippet: The farm cafe accidentally gave you change for a twenty when you only paid with a ten, and your dad already paid for the rest of the table and walked off.
options: go back to the till and return the extra change honestly
keep it because tills make mistakes and it's their problem
split the extra with dad once you reach the car park
buy a treat with the extra change to share with the family
payload.explanation: Honest returns are what you'd want if the till lost your money.

payload.snippet: The end-of-trip headcount is one short and your teacher is panicking, but you saw the missing girl sneak into the gift shop to buy a soft toy before the coach leaves.
options: tell the teacher straight away so she can fetch her quickly
run to the gift shop and grab her yourself without telling
let her catch up because she'll come out in a minute
wait quietly because telling on her would be a bit mean
payload.explanation: Telling now ends the panic and gets everyone on the coach.
